engines.name: 3.0L V6 turbo diesel (GL320 CDI/BlueTEC, GL350 BlueTEC)
4.0L twin-turbo V8 mild hybrid (GLS580, AMG GLS63, Maybach GLS600)

issues.t: Airmatic air suspension sags and the compressor wears out
issues.sym: A corner or the whole SUV sits low after parking, a suspension warning shows on the dash, or the air compressor runs for a long time.
issues.why: Every first-generation GL rides on Airmatic air suspension. With age the rubber air springs and struts crack and leak, valve blocks and lines lose air, and the compressor wears itself out trying to keep up.
issues.next: Have the leak found before paying for a compressor, or the new one will fail the same way. Don't drive far with a corner sitting on its bump stops.

issues.t: Brake booster housing can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard or inconsistent and the SUV takes longer to stop. In the worst case braking help can be lost.
issues.why: Moisture gets trapped under a rubber sleeve on the brake booster and rusts the housing. Mercedes told owners not to drive affected vehicles until they are repaired.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Stop driving it and call a Mercedes-Benz dealer with your VIN. The inspection and any booster replacement are free under recalls 22V-315 and 24V-298.

issues.t: 7-speed automatic slips, hesitates or gets stuck in gear
issues.sym: Delayed or harsh shifts, the engine revving without the SUV speeding up, or the transmission stuck in one gear until the engine is restarted. Codes such as P2767 or P2768 may be stored.
issues.why: The electronic conductor plate inside the 7-speed transmission's valve body fails, and its speed sensors can stop reading correctly.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read by a shop that knows Mercedes. Replacing and programming the conductor plate usually fixes it without a new transmission.

issues.t: Transfer case chain stretches and clunks
issues.sym: Clunking or popping from under the SUV, grinding, noise at full steering lock, or a lurch when you accelerate.
issues.why: The chain inside the 4MATIC transfer case stretches with mileage and starts slapping and skipping.
issues.next: Get it checked soon. Replacing the chain is a much smaller job than replacing the whole transfer case.

issues.t: Worn idler gear throws off engine timing
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on (often code P0017), and the engine may rattle, idle rough or misfire.
issues.why: Early V8 engines used a timing idler gear made of soft metal. Its teeth wear down and the camshaft timing drifts. Mercedes settled a class action over these gears.
issues.next: Have the engine serial number checked to see if yours has the early gear. The repair is big because the engine usually has to come out, so get a quote from a Mercedes specialist.

issues.t: Water leaks damage the SAM control modules
issues.sym: Strange electrical faults: windows moving by themselves, wipers stopping, random warning lights for the parking brake or tire pressure.
issues.why: Water gets in through the battery area, rear pillar, cabin filter box, sunroof seals or tail lights and corrodes the front and rear SAM modules and wiring.
issues.next: Check the battery first, since a weak one causes similar faults. Then find and seal the leak before replacing any modules, or the new ones will be ruined too.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from hoses, pump and radiator
issues.sym: Sweet coolant smell, drips under the front, a low coolant warning, or the heater blowing cold. It can lead to overheating.
issues.why: Plastic lines, hoses and seals get brittle with heat and age. The water pump, thermostat, turbo coolant lines and radiator are common leak points; cracked radiators and turbo lines show up more on the second generation.
issues.next: Top up only with Mercedes-approved coolant and have the leak pressure-tested. Fix it quickly; overheating can do far more damage to these engines than a bad hose.

issues.t: Door handles and lock actuators stop working
issues.sym: A door won't lock or unlock with the key fob, the touch-sensitive outside handle stops responding, or a lock button fails. The rear driver's door often goes first.
issues.why: The exterior handles wear and get weathered, and the electric lock actuators inside the doors fail.
issues.next: You can still open the door mechanically. Have the handle or actuator replaced; it's a routine door-panel job.

issues.t: Secondary air pump fails on start-up
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0410, or a loud electric whine for the first minute after a cold start.
issues.why: The secondary air injection pump, which helps warm the catalytic converters, fails, often because its relay or 40-amp fuse goes bad.
issues.next: Check the relay and fuse first, since they are simple to check. If the pump itself is dead, an aftermarket unit is an option besides a dealer part.

issues.t: Front suspension bushings and links wear and clunk
issues.sym: Squeaks or clunks from the front over bumps, or creaking from a rear corner.
issues.why: The GL is heavy, and its control arm bushings, ball joints and sway bar end links wear out with mileage.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. Worn arms and links are normal repairs, but get an alignment afterward to protect the tires.

issues.t: Driver's airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs. The danger only shows up if the airbag goes off.
issues.why: These GLs use a Takata driver's airbag inflator that can break down in heat and humidity and burst, throwing metal pieces at the driver.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-081 and get the free driver airbag replacement as soon as possible.

issues.t: Diesel fuel filter can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Diesel smell around the engine, or wet spots near the fuel filter.
issues.why: On some 2011 diesels the fuel filter can leak around its heater, and some O-rings weren't lubricated during assembly, which can also cause a leak.
issues.next: A diesel leak near hot parts is a fire risk. Have a dealer check for recalls 11V-496 and 10V-540 and fix it free.

issues.t: Diesel emissions settlement repair and extended warranty
issues.sym: Usually none. Some owners notice the emissions warning or AdBlue (DEF) messages.
issues.why: Mercedes diesels from 2009-2016 carried emissions software that regulators said was not disclosed. A 2020 settlement requires a software update and some new NOx parts, with an extended warranty on those parts.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the settlement update has been done on your VIN. It's free, and it brings extended coverage on related emissions parts.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle for a few seconds on a cold start
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine that lasts a few seconds right after a cold start, and sometimes knocking on a hot restart.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioners on this twin-turbo V8 lose oil pressure while parked. Mercedes issued a bulletin (LI05.10-P-056435) calling for new tensioners and check valves.
issues.next: Don't ignore it. Have the tensioners replaced before the chain stretches, which is a much bigger repair.

issues.t: Cylinder walls get scored, causing knocking and oil burning
issues.sym: A knock or rattle, misfires, using a lot of oil, or blue smoke from the exhaust. It tends to be worse in cold climates and more common on the GL550.
issues.why: The cylinder bore surface gets scuffed, made worse by poor lubrication on cold starts. Mild scoring may cause no trouble, but bad cases lose compression.
issues.next: Have a shop look inside the cylinders with a borescope. If scoring is severe, the fix is re-sleeving or a replacement engine, so get a second opinion.

issues.t: Timing cover leaks oil
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the front of the engine and coating parts below it. Oil loss is usually small.
issues.why: The factory sealant on the timing cover fails on this V8.
issues.next: Watch the oil level. The reseal is labor-heavy, so many owners have it done together with other engine work.

issues.t: Oil wicks from cam sensors into the engine wiring
issues.sym: Random electrical faults and a pile of trouble codes; one owner had about 20 at once. The engine may run badly.
issues.why: The camshaft position sensors leak oil, which travels inside the wiring harness and can reach and damage the engine computer.
issues.next: Check the cam sensor plugs for oil. Replace the leaking sensors early; once oil reaches the computer the repair gets much bigger.

issues.t: Steering wheel shakes when braking from highway speed
issues.sym: Vibration or shudder through the wheel and pedal when you brake, most noticeable at highway speed.
issues.why: The front rotors on second-generation GLs wear unevenly. Brake parts on this SUV are also made soft for grip, so they wear faster than on many vehicles.
issues.next: Replace rotors and pads together. If it still vibrates afterward, have the wheel bearings and suspension checked.

issues.t: Active Curve System oil can foam and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Oily residue near the Active Curve System reservoir, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: If the oil in this optional anti-roll system runs low, it can foam and push out of the cap's vent onto hot parts, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 18V-272. They will set the oil level and fit a new cap at no charge.

issues.t: Emergency call system may send the wrong location (recall)
issues.sym: Usually none until the emergency call system is used.
issues.why: A software fault can set the wrong date and time in the eCall module, so the location sent to responders may be wrong.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about recall 19V-787. The software fix is free and is often done over the air.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may switch off for an adult (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag-off light stays lit with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The seat occupant sensing system may be calibrated wrong and treat an adult like a child seat, turning the passenger airbag off.
issues.next: Get the free software update under recall 16V-903. Until then, watch the passenger airbag light.

issues.t: Water can knock out power steering assist (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, especially at low speeds.
issues.why: A poorly sealed connector lets water reach the electric power steering control unit.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 17V-241. They replace the connector and inspect the steering rack for free.

issues.t: Airbags may not deploy correctly due to software (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms.
issues.why: Wrong software in certain control units may stop the airbags from firing correctly in a crash.
issues.next: Get the free software update for recall 17V-177 at a dealer.

issues.t: Emergency call system can stop working from a SIM software error (recall)
issues.sym: An eCall or communication fault message, or no response from the SOS button.
issues.why: A software error in the SIM card can cause a network failure that disables the emergency call system.
issues.next: Ask about recall 22V-365. The update is free, over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: Backup camera can show no picture (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays blank or doesn't show the rear view when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A software error can keep the rearview camera image from showing.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look back until it's fixed. The dealer software update under recall 22V-232 is free.

issues.t: 48-volt ground connection under the passenger seat can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly a hot or burning electrical smell inside, or 48-volt system warnings. Often no signs at all.
issues.why: A ground cable bolt under the front passenger seat may not be tightened properly. Resistance builds up and the connection can overheat, raising fire risk.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recalls 22V-231 and 24V-207 for your VIN. The inspection and tightening are free.

issues.t: Engine can stall when the transmission doesn't downshift (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls as you slow down, or downshifts feel abrupt.
issues.why: In some conditions the 9-speed transmission doesn't fully downshift while slowing, which can stall the inline-six engine.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Get the free transmission software update under recall 24V-118, and ask about the other 48-volt campaigns at the same visit.

issues.t: Harsh or lumpy downshifts when slowing down
issues.sym: A noticeable bump or harsh shift as the SUV slows to a stop, often from 5th to 4th gear.
issues.why: Owners report the 9-speed's shift programming feels rough when coasting down. Dealers have applied software updates referencing a service bulletin.
issues.next: Describe exactly when it happens and ask the dealer to check for transmission software updates. Results vary, so keep notes if it comes back.

issues.t: Third-row seatbacks may not lock in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: A third-row seatback may not feel firmly latched.
issues.why: A manufacturing error can leave the third-row seatback locks unable to hold in a crash.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 22V-732. They inspect and replace the seatbacks if needed at no charge.

issues.t: Rear door window trim can come off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or a loose trim strip around the rear door windows.
issues.why: The trim bars on the rear door windows may not be secured well enough and can come off at speed.
issues.next: Get the free inspection under recalls 22V-680 and 23V-178.

issues.t: A/C drain hoses can leak water into the cabin (recall)
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the front footwell, or electrical faults after using the A/C.
issues.why: The air conditioning drain hoses may be fitted wrong, so condensation drips inside. Water can cause electrical faults, a fire risk, or loss of the emergency call system and door unlocking.
issues.next: Have the dealer check recall 23V-177 and reinstall the hoses free. Dry out any wet carpet quickly.

issues.t: Fuel pump can shut down and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: The engine loses power or stalls while driving, or won't restart.
issues.why: The fuel pump in these SUVs can stop working.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 23V-445 and 23V-880. The pump replacement is free.

issues.t: Windshield camera and mirror can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview mirror or the camera behind it feels loose or falls off, and lane-keeping or automatic braking may stop working.
issues.why: The multi-purpose camera and mirror may not be bonded firmly enough to the windshield.
issues.next: Get the free windshield replacement under recall 25V-325. Drive with extra care if the driver assists are off.

issues.t: Carbon builds up on the intake valves
issues.sym: Over time, rough idle, hesitation or a gradual loss of smoothness and power.
issues.why: This inline-six sprays fuel straight into the cylinders, so nothing washes the intake valves. Oil vapor and residue slowly bake onto them.
issues.next: Use the correct oil and change it on time. If the engine starts running rough at higher mileage, ask a shop about an intake valve cleaning.

issues.t: Rear tires wear out fast on staggered 21-inch wheels
issues.sym: Rear tires need replacing around 25,000-30,000 miles while the fronts last much longer.
issues.why: With different tire sizes front and rear, the tires can't be rotated, so the rears wear faster.
issues.next: Check rear tread depth often and plan on replacing rear tires sooner than you'd expect. Keep the alignment and pressures correct.
